items.title: ‘She can always change her mind’: Should a widow leave the family home to her stepchildren?
items.content: “It would be a less drastic step than selling the home now and splitting the proceeds.”

items.title: As AI trade falters, Goldman Sachs says this lagging region is now positioned to outperform
items.content: Precisely because it has long been hamstrung by rigid labor markets and overregulation, European stocks may paradoxically be bigger beneficiaries of the AI revolution in terms of enhanced productivity and cost-cutting than its U.S. counterparts

items.title: ‘We had the worst fight’: I want my husband to retire at 65, but I don’t want to lose his $280,000 salary. Is that unreasonable?
items.content: “We have $2.6 million, most of it in his 401(k) and IRAs, plus $450,000 in a brokerage account.”

items.title: A failed trial for a heart drug casts shadow over rivals developing similar therapies
items.content: The full data from the closely watched clinical trial showed that the drug had no cardiovascular benefit even though it reduced Lp(a) levels.

items.title: Corporate America’s profit numbers are just barely beating Wall Street’s expectations
items.content: S&P 500 companies’ earnings are mostly topping analysts’ estimates — but by the narrowest margin in roughly four years.

items.title: My 93-year-old father changed his will at the 11th hour, leaving my brother his entire $500,000 estate. Can I challenge it?
items.content: “My brother had no job and needed a place to live.”

items.title: Retirement is now part of the affordability crisis. Politicians should pay attention.
items.content: Americans are more concerned about retirement than ever, and some of their biggest fears can’t be fixed by individual behavior alone.

items.title: The biggest takeaway from Berkshire Hathaway’s latest quarter isn’t the $357 billion cash or its stock buybacks
items.content: The dismal performance of Geico is the biggest takeaway from Berkshire Hathaway’s third-quarter results.

items.title: A new setback for the AI trade: Nvidia’s board is probing CEO Huang’s relationship with an alleged spy
items.content: Jensen Huang will remain in his role and cooperate with the investigation, though analysts say the matter could cloud over Nvidia’s stock for some time.
